title: Bizarre Ways to Die
summary: Josh and Chuck count down bizarre ways to die, drawn from Chuck's HowStuffWorks article "Ten Bizarre Ways to Die." They cover a Canadian man stuck upside down in a sewer grate, a English farmer's wife knocked off a cliff by sheep and hit by a falling TV, the 1919 Boston molasses flood, the Collyer brothers (Homer and Langley) of Harlem who were compulsive hoarders, failed actress Pagan Twistle's suicide off the Hollywood sign, the 1959 Dyatlov Pass hikers in the Ural Mountains, and a English teen who died from overusing aerosol deodorant containing butane and propane. The episode closes with plugs for their spoken word album "Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy," their blog, and a listener email from Anna about living with facial blindness (prosopagnosia).
topics: Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy

segments.title: Opening banter and Chuck's cheek superstition
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show with a joke about Chuck's cheek ritual before recording, and explain that the bizarre deaths article did well on the homepage.

segments.title: Man stuck in sewer grate
segments.summary: A man from Canada in 2008 became wedged upside down in a sewer grate after going down to retrieve his wallet. He was pulled out alive by tow truck but died later, pronounced dead at the hospital. The hosts discuss the cause of death, which is unclear.

segments.title: Farmer's wife killed by sheep
segments.summary: In England, a farmer's wife going out to feed sheep was knocked off a cliff at a quarry edge by a hungry flock. A falling TV she had brought along may have contributed to her death.

segments.title: 1919 Boston molasses flood
segments.summary: In 1919 in Boston's North End, a large molasses holding tank ruptured, sending a wall of molasses roughly 25 feet high through the neighborhood at about 35 miles per hour. People were killed by shrapnel and by drowning in the molasses; cleanup took years.

segments.title: Collyer brothers and compulsive hoarding
segments.summary: Homer and Langley Collyer lived as hermits in Harlem after 1909 and became compulsive hoarders, accumulating around 180 tons of junk. Homer went blind and bedridden, and Langley was killed when a booby trap triggered an avalanche of junk. Homer apparently starved afterward. The hosts also mention brain research on hoarding.

segments.title: Pagan Twistle and the Hollywood sign
segments.summary: Failed actress Pagan Twistle, after repeated acting rejections, left a suicide note, climbed the Hollywood sign and jumped to her death in 1992. The day after she died, a letter offering her a part as a suicidal woman arrived at her house.

segments.title: Dyatlov Pass hikers in the Urals
segments.summary: A group of Russian college students hiking in the Ural Mountains in winter died mysteriously. Their tent was found cut open from inside, and bodies showed massive internal injuries without external wounds; one was missing her tongue, and some clothing had elevated radiation. Orange spheres were reportedly seen in the sky that night. The hosts discuss possible army radiation tests and the sealed case files.

segments.title: Teen dies from excessive deodorant use
segments.summary: A 16-year-old in England heavily used aerosol deodorant several times a day for about two years, inhaling and absorbing butane and propane. The levels in his system were about ten times lethal, causing heart failure. The hosts discuss how aerosols containing these propellants are no longer common.

segments.title: Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy plug
segments.summary: Hosts promote their first full-length spoken word album, Super Stuffed Guide to the Economy, available on iTunes.

segments.title: Blog plug
segments.summary: The hosts describe their blog, accessible from the HowStuffWorks homepage, where each posts about once a day.

segments.title: Listener email on facial blindness
segments.summary: Listener Anna writes about living with prosopagnosia (facial blindness), explaining she recognizes people by hair, skin color, body language, voice and typical clothing rather than faces. The hosts thank her and invite tips by email.
